title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E410 (Novi Commentarii 15, 1771) sets up a general theory of the equilibrium and motion of a thread (curve AB) that may be perfectly flexible or elastic. On the preceding page Euler replaced the action of the cut-off part AM on the point M by two forces. The first is a tangential force T along MT. The second is a normal force V applied through an imagined rigid rod at distance MV = v from M. The product Vv is the bending moment, fixed by the elastic law in terms of the curvature. For a perfectly flexible thread V = 0.

This page:
(VIII) At the neighbouring point m, with Mm = ds and tangent mt, the corresponding quantities are T+dT along mt, V+dV normal (vp), and arm mv = v+dv. These forces keep the remaining part Bm in the same state after a cut at m, just as T and V at M replace the action of AM before the cut.
(IX) T, V are equivalent to all actions of AM on M, and T+dT, V+dV are equivalent to all actions of Am. Hence the latter system must equal the former plus the external forces acting on the element Mm. Euler resolves the element load into a tangential part p ds along Mm and a normal part q ds along mr, both proportional to ds. He notes that it does not matter whether the normal load is applied at m or at M; the moment difference is second order.

Modern form: this is the Euler cut principle for a rod. It uses a contact force (tension T plus shear V) and a contact couple M = Vv, the couple being represented as a normal force with a lever arm. Balance of forces and moments on an element with distributed load (p, q) follows. On the next page this gives dT - V dφ + p ds = 0, dV + T dφ + q ds = 0 and d(Vv) = V ds, i.e. dM/ds = shear. These are the equilibrium equations of a planar Euler–Bernoulli/Kirchhoff rod.
errors: No errors in the content of this page.

Representing the contact couple by a force V at arm v is a device: only the product Vv (the moment) is determined, so V and v are not separately meaningful. Euler himself recovers this later, and the device obscures the fact that the shear force is fixed by moment balance.
Distributed applied couples on the element are tacitly excluded.

ideas.what: Cut principle: the action of a removed portion on the remainder is replaced by equivalent contact forces at the cut point.
ideas.modern_name: Euler's cut principle / contact force and contact couple in rods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (this paper, E410, 1771) per Truesdell; general Euler–Cauchy stress principle later (Cauchy 1822-23)
ideas.where_published: E410, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 15 (1771); analysed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies 1638-1788 (Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Internal force at a section decomposed into tension T and normal (shear) force V, with the bending moment as Vv.
ideas.modern_name: Tension, shear force and bending moment in a beam/rod
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler 1771 (shear force in rod theory); Jakob Bernoulli and Euler earlier for the bending moment

ideas.what: Balance of the element Mm: forces at m equal forces at M plus distributed loads p ds (tangential) and q ds (normal), with application point immaterial to first order.
ideas.modern_name: Local balance of linear momentum and moment for a rod element with distributed loads

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the well-known setup of Euler's general rod equations with shear force. Truesdell (1960) analysed and credited it extensively as a landmark, so nothing here is missing from the record.
transcription_corrections: Line 'IX. Quum igitur vires T et V respectu puncti M aequivaleant': the image shows 'aequi-valeant' (with v), consistent with the transcription. No substantive errors found; the transcription matches the image.
